European research actuators: evidence & scope

Robot Body Atlas v0.2.1 · Snapshot: 29 October 2026. This is a research catalogue, not a standardized independent benchmark or a procurement ranking.

The interface, filters and catalogue summaries support Chinese and English. Source-specific technical notes, manufacturer documents, papers, JSON downloads and the original performance workbook retain their original language. Translation does not change a numeric value, unit, evidence level or hardware revision.

How coverage was selected

This selection uses public papers, university platforms and manufacturer case studies. It is not a statistical survey of European market share or a claim that any brand is the most common.

The actuator catalogue includes complete joint modules, smart servos and motor-only records. European research coverage includes MAB Robotics, historical ANYdrive/SEA evidence, HEBI modules, maxon, TQ frameless motors and FAULHABER motor use in iCub wrist research, alongside internationally used CubeMars and DYNAMIXEL products.

ANYbotics and MAB Robotics

Historical ANYdrive publications document research actuator specifications and robot-level SEA work. They do not establish current retail availability or the specifications of every current ANYmal joint. Read the availability and version notes for each record. MAB Robotics offers integrated actuators and has public research/adoption evidence; that evidence supports inclusion, not a Europe-wide usage ranking.

Motor-only versus complete joint values

A frameless motor’s torque is motor-shaft torque and its mass may include only rotor and stator. It does not include a complete drive, gearbox or housing. Complete joint values refer to the listed output. Use the integration filter before comparing torque density or mass.

Research adoption links

Brand adoption does not prove a specific part number or installation at every axis. Research, manufacturer and historical evidence are identified separately in each detail view. Verify hardware revision, drive, transmission and cooling conditions before making an engineering comparison.
